intro: Detroit ended Minnesota's perfect start, Chicago is a half game behind the Vikings after Monday night, and the Jaguars visit the Ravens tonight on Prime Video. Seattle turns to Drew Lock this weekend while Pittsburgh heads into its bye on a four-game win streak. 160 stories across all 32 teams.

top.label: Biggest Story
top.headline: Lions hand Vikings their first loss, 19-15
top.dek: Jameson Williams caught a 7-yard touchdown from Jared Goff in the fourth quarter to decide it at Ford Field. Detroit ran for 230 yards, moved to 5-2 and is 2-0 in the division. Minnesota drops to 6-1.

top.label: Injury Watch
top.headline: Sam Darnold out Sunday, Drew Lock to start for Seattle
top.dek: Darnold will miss the game at Arizona with quad and rib injuries. Lock steps in after a 34-17 Monday night loss to Chicago. Seattle is 4-4.

top.label: Player Spotlight
top.headline: Jaylen Warren runs for 143 yards as Steelers win again
top.dek: Warren carried 17 times for 143 yards and a touchdown against Cleveland. He has 704 rushing yards, 5.9 yards per carry and seven touchdowns. Pittsburgh has won four straight.

top.label: Stat of the Day
top.headline: 1 for 11: Seattle's third-down mark against the Bears
top.dek: Chicago held the Seahawks to one conversion on 11 tries and 252 total yards. Seattle ran for 81 yards, and D'Andre Swift scored three second-half touchdowns on short runs.

top.label: What's Next
top.headline: Mayfield brings the Bucs to Soldier Field on Sunday night
top.dek: Tampa Bay (3-5) plays at Chicago (6-2) on Sunday, Nov. 8 at 8:20 p.m. ET on NBC. Caleb Williams and Baker Mayfield meet for the first time. Bucky Irving ranks fourth in the NFL with 728 rushing yards, so watch the Bears' run defense.

teams.name: Buffalo Bills
teams.headline: Allen passes Kelly as Bills hit 6-1

stories.text: Josh Allen passes Jim Kelly for the Bills touchdown record
stories.summary: Allen threw two touchdown passes in a 36-10 win over Baltimore on Sunday, one to DJ Moore, and took the franchise touchdown record from Jim Kelly. He also ran in the opening score on a one-yard sneak. The Bills are 6-1 and have won three straight.

stories.text: Moore, Palmer and Brown all listed with injuries before Minnesota
stories.summary: Receiver DJ Moore has a knee issue and an AC joint sprain after leaving the Baltimore game early. Joshua Palmer pulled a right hamstring and Spencer Brown (back) sat out Sunday. All three had no status set as of Tuesday night. Cornerback Jordan Hancock returned to practice Wednesday from a Week 2 hamstring injury.

stories.text: Greg Rousseau terrorizes Baltimore with a sack and three hits
stories.summary: Rousseau had a sack, three quarterback hits, at least seven pressures and two passes defended against the Ravens. Eight Buffalo defenders got to the quarterback in a game that produced four sacks and 12 hits. Rookies Landon Jackson and TJ Parker each recorded their first career sacks.

stories.text: 21: straight field goals for Tyler Bass, a Bills record
stories.summary: Bass made all three of his kicks against Baltimore, from 56, 22 and 51 yards. That stretch of 21 straight made field goals sets a Bills regular-season record. Buffalo also went 4 of 14 on third down and took 10 penalties, and still won by 26.

stories.text: Bills visit Vikings on Monday night in a battle of 6-1 teams
stories.summary: Buffalo plays at Minnesota on Monday, Nov. 9, at 8:15 p.m. ET on ESPN/ABC. Both teams are 6-1. Minnesota has the league's top defense by EPA per play, while Buffalo's offense leads the league in that measure. Watch the Vikings quarterback situation, since Kyler Murray is dealing with a hamstring problem.

teams.name: Miami Dolphins
teams.headline: Chop Robinson trade talk heats up before deadline

stories.text: Dolphins weigh Chop Robinson calls ahead of Nov. 10 deadline
stories.summary: Teams that need pass rush are expected to pursue edge rusher Chop Robinson, according to reports from ESPN's Adam Schefter and Ian Rapoport. Miami views the 23-year-old as part of its future, but general manager Jon-Eric Sullivan will listen to offers. The deadline is Nov. 10 and the Dolphins are 1-6.

stories.text: Proctor in concussion protocol, Herring has neck stinger
stories.summary: Tackle Kadyn Proctor has a concussion and sat out the loss to New England. Defensive end Malik Herring suffered a neck stinger Sunday but came back in the third quarter. Running back De'Von Achane is on injured reserve with a torn ACL, and cornerback Storm Duck is on IR with a knee injury.

stories.text: Malik Willis throws two touchdowns but absorbs five sacks
stories.summary: Willis went 21 of 32 for 211 yards, two touchdowns and an interception in the 24-19 loss to New England. His 35-yard touchdown to rookie Kevin Coleman Jr. came with two minutes left. Miami led 13-3 at the half and scored only once after that.

stories.text: 0-3: Miami's record at Hard Rock Stadium this season
stories.summary: The Dolphins are winless at home and have lost to the Patriots by five after leading by 10 at halftime. They beat the Jets on the road the week before for their lone win. Detroit arrives Sunday at 5-2 and riding a three-game winning streak.

stories.text: Dolphins host the Lions on Sunday at 1 p.m. ET on FOX
stories.summary: Detroit brings running back Jahmyr Gibbs, who has 773 rushing yards and eight rushing touchdowns through seven games. The Lions have injury questions on defense, including Jack Campbell, listed as doubtful. Miami looks for its first home win.

teams.name: New England Patriots
teams.headline: Brown and Henry miss practice before Packers

stories.text: Patriots wait on A.J. Brown and Hunter Henry before Green Bay
stories.summary: Brown, who has a knee issue, did not practice Wednesday and missed the win in Miami. Henry left that game with a foot injury and also sat out. Mike Vrabel gave no timeline for Brown. Drake Maye called Henry a security blanket and said losing him would hurt the offense.

stories.text: Four sit out Wednesday, Hollins and Van Roten practice
stories.summary: Brown (ankle, knee), Henry (foot), running back TreVeyon Henderson (illness) and tackle Christian Barmore (illness) did not practice Wednesday. Wide receiver Mack Hollins (calf) and guard Greg Van Roten (hamstring) were limited and could return from injured reserve. Maye, who has a right shoulder issue, took full reps.

stories.text: Drake Maye keeps rolling with a three-touchdown comeback
stories.summary: Maye went 16 of 20 for 199 yards, threw two touchdown passes and ran for another in the 24-19 win over Miami. It was his fifth straight game with at least three total touchdowns. New England trailed 13-3 at the half and scored 21 straight in the second half.

stories.text: -7: New England's turnover differential, 31st in the NFL
stories.summary: The Patriots are 5-3 despite the second-worst turnover margin in the league. Green Bay, by contrast, is plus-4 and tied for seventh. New England is eighth in total offense at 367.3 yards a game and ninth in points allowed at 20.3.

stories.text: Packers visit Gillette on Sunday at 4:25 p.m. ET on FOX
stories.summary: Both teams are 5-3. Green Bay has the league's second-ranked passing offense at 271.0 yards a game but ranks last in rushing at 60.6. Rob Gronkowski goes into the Patriots Hall of Fame Saturday and gets a halftime honor Sunday. Tom Brady will call the game for FOX.

teams.name: New York Jets
teams.headline: Glenn defends Jets after third straight loss

stories.text: Glenn says he is not worried about his job at 2-6
stories.summary: The Jets blew a fourth-quarter lead in a 38-33 loss to Las Vegas, their third straight defeat. Coach Aaron Glenn, now 5-20 with the team, said he is focused on fixing the roster and noted nine games remain. Special teams gave up a 95-yard kickoff return touchdown, the first in the NFL this season.

stories.text: Breece Hall limited Wednesday and trending toward a return
stories.summary: Hall has missed five straight games with a right quad injury he first suffered in the Week 3 loss to Detroit. He was limited in Wednesday's practice, and the team has not set a game designation. Glenn said Hall and Braelon Allen will both play if Hall is cleared. The Jets say they will not trade Hall before the Nov. 10 deadline.

stories.text: Braelon Allen runs for a career-high 147 yards
stories.summary: Filling in for Hall, Allen carried 21 times for 147 yards and a touchdown against the Raiders, with 121 of those yards in the first half. His 21-yard touchdown run put the Jets up 30-21 in the third quarter. He has topped 100 yards in three of his last four games.

stories.text: 107-9: Jets' scoring margin in last two minutes of first halves
stories.summary: Under Glenn, opponents have outscored the Jets 107-9 in the final two minutes before halftime. The Jets also went 2 of 6 in the red zone against Las Vegas and settled for four field goals. They have lost five of six games by one score this season.

stories.text: Jets visit Chiefs on Sunday at 1 p.m. ET on CBS
stories.summary: Kansas City is 5-2 after back-to-back losses to Seattle and Denver. New York's rushing attack, which gained 166 yards against Las Vegas, faces a defense allowing 18.7 points a game. Buffalo visits MetLife Stadium on Nov. 15.

teams.name: Baltimore Ravens
teams.headline: Fagnano starts as Brissett trade nears

stories.text: Ravens add Brissett, but Fagnano starts tonight
stories.summary: Baltimore is finalizing a trade with Arizona for Jacoby Brissett after injuries to Lamar Jackson and Tyler Huntley. The deal should close this weekend, too late for tonight. Undrafted rookie Joe Fagnano starts against Jacksonville, and Brissett is slated to take over in Week 10.

stories.text: Jackson headed to IR, Huntley and Loop also hurt
stories.summary: Jackson hurt his right thumb on the first snap against Buffalo and will have surgery and go on injured reserve. Huntley left with a toe injury, and kicker Tyler Loop (groin) missed practice, which could put Jake Moody in line to kick. Cornerback Nate Wiggins returned to walkthrough after a stinger. Statuses are from Monday's practice report, so check tonight's inactives.

stories.text: Fagnano gets first NFL start after relief debut
stories.summary: Fagnano finished the Buffalo loss 10 of 21 for 91 yards with one interception, and said he expects to be ready tonight. He made 44 starts at UConn and threw 48 touchdowns to 6 interceptions there. He is playing with an ankle brace after taking a low hit from Bills lineman Ed Oliver.

stories.text: 7-13: Ravens record all-time without Lamar Jackson
stories.summary: Baltimore has won seven and lost 13 in games Jackson misses. The Ravens are 4-4 and riding a three-game losing streak, and they are 2-6 against the spread. Jackson will miss at least the next four games, starting tonight.

stories.text: Ravens host Jaguars tonight, 8:15 ET on Prime Video
stories.summary: Baltimore (4-4) hosts Jacksonville (5-2) at M&T Bank Stadium. Watch whether Derrick Henry can top 60 rushing yards for the first time in four games against the league's top run defense. Next Gen Stats puts the Ravens' playoff odds at 20%, down from 70% four weeks ago.

teams.name: Cincinnati Bengals
teams.headline: Burrow's 462 yards beat Titans in OT

stories.text: Bengals outlast Titans 43-36 in overtime
stories.summary: Joe Burrow threw for 462 yards and five touchdowns, then ran in the winner in overtime. Cincinnati moved to 5-2. Boye Mafe's strip-sack set up one Burrow score, and Dexter Lawrence added a sack and a fumble recovery.

stories.text: Howell, Johnson, Turner questionable for Madrid
stories.summary: Defensive end Cashius Howell, defensive end Cedric Johnson and cornerback DJ Turner II carry questionable tags for Sunday. Receiver Andrei Iosivas is on injured reserve. Reports conflict on Howell: one lists him questionable, while the team site shows a reserve/injured move for a wrist injury.

stories.text: Higgins posts 155 yards and two scores
stories.summary: Tee Higgins caught 10 passes for 155 yards and two touchdowns in the overtime win. Ja'Marr Chase added 11 catches for 141 yards and a score. Mike Gesicki's fourth-quarter touchdown put Cincinnati ahead 29-28.

stories.text: 302.1: Burrow's passing yards per game lead the NFL
stories.summary: Burrow also leads quarterbacks with a 73% completion rate and 20 touchdown passes. Cincinnati ranks third in offensive weighted EPA per play. Those numbers came before his 462-yard day against Tennessee.

stories.text: Bengals meet Falcons in Madrid, Sunday 9:30 AM ET
stories.summary: Cincinnati (5-2) plays Atlanta (3-5) at the Santiago Bernabeu on NFL Network. The Falcons come off a 16-0 loss to Tampa Bay. After the trip, the Bengals host Pittsburgh in Week 10 with the AFC North lead in play.

teams.name: Cleveland Browns
teams.headline: Watson in protocol, Sanders may start

stories.text: Watson in concussion protocol, Sanders prepping
stories.summary: Deshaun Watson took a helmet hit against Pittsburgh, returned to the game, and reported symptoms Monday night. Shedeur Sanders took first-team reps Wednesday and starts if Watson is not cleared. Cleveland is 5-3 after the 27-6 loss to the Steelers.

stories.text: Jenkins on IR, Howard cleared, Harden and Thomas limited
stories.summary: Guard Teven Jenkins went on injured reserve with a back injury and misses at least four games. Right tackle Tytus Howard cleared concussion protocol and played in Pittsburgh. Cornerback Myles Harden (hamstring) and safety Daniel Thomas (ankle) were limited ahead of that game. Linebacker Jeremiah Owusu-Koramoah remains on PUP with a neck injury. This report predates the Watson news.

stories.text: Fannin Jr. catches 10 for 154 in a losing game
stories.summary: Harold Fannin Jr. was the best Browns offensive player in Pittsburgh, with 10 catches for 154 yards and a 76.4 PFF grade. He also lost a fumble after a short catch in the fourth quarter. Jerry Jeudy had one target and no catch.

stories.text: 33: sacks Watson has taken, most in the NFL
stories.summary: Watson has completed 65.5% of his passes for 1,806 yards with seven touchdowns and three interceptions. Pittsburgh sacked him eight times on Sunday. Cleveland's offensive line is the story behind the 5-3 record.

stories.text: Browns visit Saints Sunday, 1 PM ET on CBS
stories.summary: Cleveland (5-3) plays at the Caesars Superdome against New Orleans (2-5). The team lists kickoff at noon Central. Watch the quarterback decision and whether the line holds up after eight sacks.

teams.name: Pittsburgh Steelers
teams.headline: Steelers lead North heading into bye

stories.text: Steelers beat Browns 27-6, take AFC North lead
stories.summary: Pittsburgh is 6-2 and sits alone in first place heading into its bye. Aaron Rodgers called the win incomplete, since the offense went 4 of 11 on third down and kicked two red-zone field goals. The defense played well, and the Steelers gained 361 yards.

stories.text: Pittman running again as bye week heals receivers
stories.summary: Michael Pittman Jr. has a foot injury and has missed four games on injured reserve. He has started running and wants to return after the bye, but says he will wait until he can be effective. Running back Rico Dowdle is back from injury and producing next to Jaylen Warren.

stories.text: Warren runs for 143 and leads the offense
stories.summary: Jaylen Warren carried 17 times for 143 yards and a touchdown against Cleveland. He has 704 rushing yards, 5.9 yards per carry and seven touchdowns, on pace for his best season. Pittsburgh has won four straight.

stories.text: 8: sacks of Deshaun Watson by the Steelers
stories.summary: T.J. Watt had two sacks, and Patrick Queen and Cam Heyward each had 1.5. Watt also leads the team with 7.5 sacks on the season. Pittsburgh recovered a first-quarter Watson fumble.

stories.text: Steelers on bye, then visit Bengals in Week 10
stories.summary: Pittsburgh rests this week at 6-2. The next game is at Cincinnati (5-2), a rematch of the Steelers' Week 3 win. If the Bengals beat Atlanta in Madrid, the game decides control of the division.

teams.name: Houston Texans
teams.headline: Texans hit L.A. at 2-5 after the bye

stories.text: Texans return from the bye at 2-5 and need cleaner offense
stories.summary: C.J. Stroud said the week away helped him recharge, and he put the focus on explosive plays, fewer negative plays and fewer penalties. He credited coordinator Nick Caley for playing aggressively and praised Tank Dell after his long layoff. Houston has dropped close games, and Stroud wants the small details fixed starting in meetings.

stories.text: Noel to injured reserve with turf toe, out for the season
stories.summary: Receiver Jaylin Noel went on injured reserve October 28 after hurting his toe on a fourth-quarter kick return against the Giants. He led Houston with 331 receiving yards and averaged 17.4 yards a catch. The Texans signed running back Emari Demercado to fill the roster spot, and Tank Dell, back in Week 7 after 22 months out, picks up more work.

stories.text: Stroud ranks sixth among QBs despite the 2-5 start
stories.summary: C.J. Stroud has completed 64.8 percent of his passes for 1,867 yards and 11 touchdowns through seven games. He averages 7.6 yards an attempt and has thrown one interception. NFL.com's Week 9 quarterback rankings put him sixth and say he has played better than the record shows.

stories.text: 3.5: Woody Marks' yards per carry as the run game struggles
stories.summary: Marks has 271 rushing yards on 77 carries, a 3.5 average. That leaves Stroud carrying most of the offense, with Noel now on injured reserve. Athlon Sports points to the lack of a ground game as a reason Houston keeps asking its quarterback to do it all.

stories.text: At the Chargers, Sunday 4:05 p.m. ET on CBS
stories.summary: Houston visits SoFi Stadium in Inglewood for a 1:05 p.m. PT kickoff, which is 4:05 p.m. ET, on CBS. Watch whether Stroud finds Nico Collins and Dell for big plays against a defense that Stroud says has made plays against good offenses. The Chargers lead the all-time series 6-4.

teams.name: Indianapolis Colts
teams.headline: Colts sell as Taylor trade looms

stories.text: Colts sell off veterans after firing Ballard, Taylor likely next
stories.summary: Owner Carlie Irsay-Gordon fired general manager Chris Ballard after ten seasons, and Ed Dodds is expected to run the front office on an interim basis. Indianapolis then traded Quenton Nelson to Seattle and DeForest Buckner to San Francisco. Running back Jonathan Taylor remains on the roster, and the trade deadline is November 10.

stories.text: Colts light on injury news as Jones stays the starter
stories.summary: Nickel cornerback Justin Walley sat out the 42-7 loss at Jacksonville. Daniel Jones is healthy and will start Sunday against Dallas, coach Shane Steichen said, though Jones could be benched if his play does not improve. The sources we read did not include a Week 9 Colts injury report yet.

stories.text: Taylor's quiet day in Jacksonville fuels the trade talk
stories.summary: Jonathan Taylor ran eight times for 23 yards against the Jaguars and fumbled on a failed trick play. He had 492 rushing yards and seven touchdowns through six games before that, and he signed an extension in August. Taylor has said he is not focused on a trade.

stories.text: 9: Daniel Jones' interceptions against five touchdowns
stories.summary: Jones has thrown nine interceptions and five touchdown passes in eight games, averaging 5.8 yards an attempt. NFL.com ranks him 31st among quarterbacks and asks whether the rebuilding Colts will bench or trade him. He went 19 of 28 for 144 yards and two picks against Jacksonville, then gave way to Anthony Richardson in the fourth quarter.

stories.text: Cowboys visit Sunday at 1 p.m. ET on FOX
stories.summary: Indianapolis hosts Dallas at Lucas Oil Stadium on November 8. The Cowboys are 3-5 and the Colts 2-6. Watch whether Taylor and receiver Josh Downs are still in the building by kickoff, with the deadline two days later.

teams.name: Jacksonville Jaguars
teams.headline: Jaguars lead South by three, face TNF

stories.text: Jaguars thump Colts 42-7 and take a three-game South lead
stories.summary: Jacksonville led 28-0 at halftime and rushed for a season-best 183 yards. Trevor Lawrence threw three touchdowns on 14 attempts, and Rayuan Lane III returned an interception 92 yards for a score. The Jaguars have won seven straight regular-season home games, each by 17 or more points, and now play Thursday night in Baltimore.

stories.text: Hamilton and Murray on IR, Walker and Tuten questionable
stories.summary: Defensive tackle DaVon Hamilton and safety Eric Murray went on injured reserve after the Colts game. Defensive end Travon Walker (ribs) is questionable, and coach Liam Coen called running back Bhayshul Tuten (ankle, foot) a game-time decision. Guard Ezra Cleveland, limited with knee and ankle issues, will play, and safety Antonio Johnson is back.

stories.text: Tuten leads the offense in scrimmage yards and touchdowns
stories.summary: Bhayshul Tuten has 673 scrimmage yards and six total touchdowns, tops on the team. He ran for 104 yards and scored on a 39-yard run against the Colts, then added a screen-pass score. His ankle and foot injury kept him out of practice three days this week.

stories.text: 17: Trevor Lawrence's touchdown passes against four interceptions
stories.summary: Lawrence has 1,690 passing yards, 17 touchdowns and four interceptions in seven games, averaging 8.5 yards an attempt. NFL.com keeps him seventh in its quarterback rankings after the Colts game. He threw three touchdowns on just 14 attempts and left early in the fourth quarter.

stories.text: At the Ravens, tonight 8:15 p.m. ET on Prime Video
stories.summary: Jacksonville (5-2) plays at M&T Bank Stadium against Baltimore (4-4). Lamar Jackson is out with a thumb injury and the Ravens may start Joe Fagnano, who is undrafted. Ezra Cleveland and Tuten's status are worth watching for a Jaguars team on a short week.

teams.name: Tennessee Titans
teams.headline: Titans on bye after near upset in OT

stories.text: Ward posts a career-best 304 yards in 43-36 overtime loss
stories.summary: Cam Ward went 26 of 40 for 304 yards and two touchdowns with no interceptions, his first 300-yard game, in the loss at Cincinnati. Tennessee led 13-0 after one quarter before Joe Burrow won it in overtime. The Titans now sit at 1-7 and use their Week 9 bye to regroup.

stories.text: Rookie receiver Tate expected back after the bye
stories.summary: Carnell Tate missed the Bengals game with a shoulder injury, and Paul Kuharsky reported he should return for the Titans' Week 10 game. Tate leads the team with 34 catches for 413 yards and one touchdown through seven games. Ward threw without him, spreading targets to Wan'Dale Robinson, Calvin Ridley and Elic Ayomanor.

stories.text: Hooker intercepts Burrow three times in the loss
stories.summary: Safety Amani Hooker had three interceptions against Cincinnati, and the Titans forced four turnovers in all, including a fumble recovery. Burrow still threw for nearly 500 yards and five touchdowns, then ran in the winning score in overtime. Hooker's day gave Tennessee a lead that its defense could not protect.

stories.text: 6.0: Cam Ward's yards per attempt through eight games
stories.summary: Ward has 1,483 passing yards, six touchdowns and five interceptions in eight games, with a 62.5 completion percentage. He also has 112 rushing yards and two rushing scores. NFL.com moved him up 15 spots to 15th in its Week 9 quarterback rankings after the Bengals game.

stories.text: Bye in Week 9, then the Jaguars on Nov. 15 at 1 p.m. ET on FOX
stories.summary: Tennessee is off this weekend. Its next game is Week 10 against Jacksonville, listed for Sunday, November 15 at noon Central on FOX. Watch Tate's return and whether the offense keeps the pace it showed in Cincinnati.

teams.name: Denver Broncos
teams.headline: Broncos take AFC West lead from Chiefs

stories.text: Broncos rally past Chiefs 28-24 to take the AFC West lead
stories.summary: Denver trailed 24-13 entering the fourth quarter and scored the last 15 points. Bo Nix hit Nate Adkins for a 2-yard touchdown, then Jonah Coleman scored from 5 yards with 1:56 left. Malcolm Roach sacked Patrick Mahomes on fourth-and-goal on the final play, and the Broncos moved to 6-2.

stories.text: Four Broncos sat out Wednesday, three of them in the secondary
stories.summary: Safeties Brandon Jones (hamstring) and Talanoa Hufanga (ankle), cornerback Kris Abrams-Draine (ankle) and lineman Eyioma Uwazurike (shoulder) did not practice. Receivers Jaylen Waddle (chest) and Pat Bryant (ankle) were full participants. Zach Allen and Courtland Sutton were limited for rest.

stories.text: Rookie Jonah Coleman supplies the winning score against Kansas City
stories.summary: Coleman turned a Nix pass into a 51-yard gain in the fourth quarter, then ran in the go-ahead touchdown from 5 yards. He finished with 104 scrimmage yards, a career best. Denver now sits at 6-2 with four straight wins.

stories.text: 2-for-11: Denver's third-down line in a win that needed none of it
stories.summary: The Broncos converted two of 11 third downs and finished under 300 total yards, yet erased an 11-point fourth-quarter deficit. It was the third comeback of that size in Nix's career. Nix finished 20 of 32 for 222 yards and two touchdowns.

stories.text: Broncos visit Panthers Sunday, then head into their bye
stories.summary: Denver plays at Carolina on Sunday at 1 p.m. ET on CBS. A win sends the Broncos into the bye at 7-2. The Panthers have lost two straight and fired defensive coordinator Ejiro Evero, so watch how interim coordinator Todd Wash changes the looks early.

teams.name: Kansas City Chiefs
teams.headline: Chiefs blow 11-point lead, lose division lead

stories.text: Chiefs lose the AFC West lead after a fourth-quarter collapse in Denver
stories.summary: Kansas City led by 11 in the second half and scored nothing in the final 15 minutes. Andy Reid punted on fourth-and-inches near midfield, Mahomes took a sack that led to a missed 54-yard field goal, and a false start wiped out a late touchdown to Rashee Rice. The 11 penalties for 105 yards were a season high.

stories.text: Rookie lineman Peter Woods sits out with a neck stinger
stories.summary: Woods left the Denver game in the first half and missed Wednesday's practice. His status for Sunday is unclear, and Chris Jones and Khyiris Tonga would likely absorb his snaps. Neck issues also put him on the report ahead of Week 6.

stories.text: Emmett Johnson breaks loose for 128 yards in a losing effort
stories.summary: Johnson caught five passes for 128 yards, including a 73-yard catch-and-run touchdown in the second quarter. Mahomes threw for 321 yards and three touchdowns, spreading the ball to nine targets. Johnson's score gave Kansas City a 14-6 lead at the time.

stories.text: 16: kicks Harrison Butker has missed since the start of last season
stories.summary: That total is the most in the NFL over that span, and it includes the 54-yard miss in Denver. Reid confirmed Butker will be active against the Jets even though the Chiefs signed Justin Tucker to the practice squad. Butker said the kick felt bad off his foot.

stories.text: Chiefs host the Jets Sunday looking to reset
stories.summary: Kansas City plays New York on Sunday at 1 p.m. ET on CBS. Reid said guard Kingsley Suamataia has a good chance to return, and cornerback Mansoor Delane was back at practice. Watch Butker and the penalty count.

teams.name: Las Vegas Raiders
teams.headline: Raiders snap four-game skid, reach .500

stories.text: Raiders end a four-game skid with a 38-33 win over the Jets
stories.summary: Las Vegas trailed by nine at halftime, scored on its first drive after the break and then added more touchdowns in a strong third quarter. The Raiders had scored three points in their previous four third quarters combined. The win moved them to 4-4.

stories.text: Cornerback Darien Porter misses Wednesday practice with a groin injury
stories.summary: Porter, a starting corner, missed all but one play against the Jets. Jackson Powers-Johnson and Patrick Johnson also did not practice. Brock Bowers, Quay Walker, Kwity Paye and Jack Bech were full, and tight end Carter Runyon was activated from injured reserve.

stories.text: Brock Bowers scores twice and gives Kirk Cousins a target
stories.summary: Bowers caught seven of 10 targets for 92 yards and two touchdowns at MetLife Stadium. Cousins went 19 of 26 for 247 yards and three touchdowns with no turnovers. Jeremy Chinn sealed it with an end-zone interception with seven seconds left.

stories.text: 221: points the Raiders have scored through eight games
stories.summary: That is their most through eight games since 2002, according to NFL.com's Week 8 review. The offense hit a season high of 38 against the Jets, even though the ground game produced 83 yards from Mike Washington Jr. and just nine from Ashton Jeanty.

stories.text: Raiders visit the 49ers Sunday afternoon
stories.summary: Las Vegas plays at San Francisco on Sunday at 4:25 p.m. ET on Fox. The 49ers lost 29-20 at Atlanta in Week 7 after a 6-0 start and have Christian McCaffrey, Mike Evans and Deebo Samuel on the injury list. Las Vegas ranks 31st in rushing and next-to-last in points allowed at 28.8 per game.

teams.name: Los Angeles Chargers
teams.headline: Chargers fall to 0-7 after loss to Rams

stories.text: Chargers drop to 0-7 with a 24-9 loss to the Rams
stories.summary: Los Angeles led 9-3 and then gave up 21 straight points. Justin Herbert threw two interceptions, one returned 45 yards by Quentin Lake. The Chargers are the first team to lose its first seven games after winning at least 11 the year before.

stories.text: Perryman and Njoku open their practice windows
stories.summary: Linebacker Denzel Perryman and tight end David Njoku began their 21-day windows to return from injured reserve. Neither has been activated yet. The Chargers listed no other new injuries in the coverage reviewed.

stories.text: Justin Herbert is leading the league in interceptions
stories.summary: Herbert threw for 257 yards, two interceptions and no touchdowns against the Rams. Through seven games he has five touchdowns, 10 interceptions and 23 sacks taken. Jim Harbaugh defended his quarterback on Wednesday and said only two throws bothered him.

stories.text: 14.1: points per game, last in the NFL
stories.summary: The Chargers have not scored a touchdown since the third quarter of Week 5. They also lead the league with 17 turnovers and rank last in EPA per play. The Athletic projects the No. 2 pick in the 2027 draft as their most likely landing spot.

stories.text: Chargers host the Texans Sunday looking for win No. 1
stories.summary: Los Angeles plays Houston on Sunday at 4:05 p.m. ET on CBS. The Texans were 2-5 heading into their bye, and they beat the Chargers in the 2024 playoffs and in Week 17 of 2025. Watch whether the offense finds a touchdown after a long drought.

teams.name: Dallas Cowboys
teams.headline: Jones backs Schottenheimer after OT collapse

stories.text: Jones rules out coaching change after Cowboys blow 17-3 lead
stories.summary: Dallas lost 33-30 in overtime to Arizona after leading 17-3, and the defense gave up 337 yards in the stretch after the Cardinals changed quarterbacks. Owner Jerry Jones has said he will not change coaches during the season. The trade deadline is the next point where he could act on a defense that national power rankings now place outside the top 20.

stories.text: Downs and Locke in concussion protocol, Ferguson out of practice
stories.summary: Safeties Caleb Downs (concussion, ankle) and P.J. Locke (concussion) did not practice Wednesday, and tight end Jake Ferguson (ankle) sat out as well. George Pickens (hamstring), Tyler Smith (ankle), Luke Schoonmaker (groin) and Dee Winters (calf) were limited. Kenny Clark, Joey Porter Jr. and Jonathan Bullard practiced fully.

stories.text: Pickens has 39 catches but only two against Arizona
stories.summary: George Pickens has 39 catches for 533 yards and two touchdowns through eight games, yet he caught just two passes for 48 yards against the Cardinals. Jerry Jones has said publicly that the team needs to get him the ball more. CeeDee Lamb leads the group with 709 yards and six touchdowns.

stories.text: 152.8: rushing yards per game Dallas allows, last in the NFL
stories.summary: No defense in the league gives up more on the ground, and Colts back Jonathan Taylor arrives with 610 yards and eight touchdowns on 148 carries. Dallas is also 1-11 under Brian Schottenheimer when it scores fewer than 30 points. The Cowboys are 3-2 when they hit 30.

stories.text: At Colts, Sunday 1 p.m. ET on Fox
stories.summary: Dallas visits Indianapolis (2-6), which has lost four straight and fell 42-7 to Jacksonville last week. Watch the Dallas secondary, which may be without both Downs and Locke, and how the Cowboys handle Taylor. The Colts also face trade noise around Taylor and receiver Josh Downs ahead of the Nov. 10 deadline.

teams.name: New York Giants
teams.headline: Giants lead the East and visit a skidding Eagles team

stories.text: Giants take NFC East lead into the bye and a trip to Philadelphia
stories.summary: New York gained ground without playing, as Dallas lost in overtime and Washington beat Philadelphia. The Giants now visit an Eagles team on a six-game losing streak, but Philadelphia has won 13 of 17 meetings since 2016 and every game at Lincoln Financial Field since 2013. Conor Orr moved the Giants up two spots to No. 15 in his power rankings.

stories.text: Skattebo and Carter miss Wednesday practice
stories.summary: Running back Cam Skattebo (hamstring) and outside linebacker Abdul Carter (illness) did not practice Wednesday, and John Harbaugh listed both as day-to-day. Andrew Thomas, Jermaine Eluemunor, Malik Harrison, Colton Hood and Charlie Jones were limited. Running back Tyrone Tracy Jr. is on injured reserve and will miss at least four more games.

stories.text: McCarthy says he is caught up after the bye
stories.summary: J.J. McCarthy has completed 31 of 49 passes for 495 yards with one touchdown and one interception in two games since arriving from Minnesota. Harbaugh said the quarterback is pretty much caught up on the playbook after the bye and extra practices. McCarthy now makes his first NFC East start.

stories.text: 13: straight Giants losses in Philadelphia
stories.summary: New York has not won at the Eagles' stadium since 2013, and the streak includes a playoff loss. The Eagles have the league's 30th-ranked scoring offense at 17.1 points per game and the worst total offense at 265.3 yards. Harbaugh called the Giants' division lead meaningless with 10 games left.

stories.text: At Eagles, Sunday 1 p.m. ET on Fox
stories.summary: The Giants go to Philadelphia fresh off the bye, then host Washington on Thursday night, Nov. 13. Watch the Giants' pass defense, which cornerback Greg Newsome II said ranks third in the league, against first-time starter Joe Milton. Also watch how Philadelphia handles a Giants offense that wants to run early.

teams.name: Philadelphia Eagles
teams.headline: Eagles bench McKee, start Joe Milton

stories.text: Eagles switch to Joe Milton at quarterback
stories.summary: Philadelphia will start Milton, who signed from Dallas' practice squad less than a month ago, over Tanner McKee for Sunday's game against the Giants. McKee went 0-3 as the starter. Players learned of the change in a Wednesday team meeting, two days after Nick Sirianni backed McKee.

stories.text: Barkley, Smith and Wicks miss Wednesday practice
stories.summary: Saquon Barkley (hamstring and back) played only 22 snaps last Sunday and sat out Wednesday. DeVonta Smith (hamstring) and Dontayvion Wicks (ankle) have missed two games each and are likely out a third. Linebacker Jihaad Campbell (hamstring and quad) missed the Washington game, and Jonathan Jones, Britain Covey and Michael Carter were also out of the early session.

stories.text: Barkley is grinding through a down stretch
stories.summary: Barkley and Elijah Mitchell combined for 64 yards on 24 carries, 2.7 per attempt, in the 27-10 loss to Washington. Philadelphia as a team gained 268 yards and averaged 3.1 yards per rush. Barkley returned after missing two games and remains limited.

stories.text: 32nd: where the Eagles rank in total offense
stories.summary: Philadelphia gains 265.3 yards per game and scores 17.1 points per game, 30th in the league. The Eagles scored 7, 20, 17, 14, 21 and 10 points during the six-game losing streak, their longest since 2012. The defense has also allowed 100 or more rushing yards in all eight games.

stories.text: Vs. Giants, Sunday 1 p.m. ET on Fox
stories.summary: The Eagles host the first-place Giants (4-2-1) at Lincoln Financial Field. Milton has thrown 53 NFL passes, all in relief, and has never started. Watch Barkley's and Smith's practice status Friday, and whether the line holds up after Washington sacked McKee five times.

teams.name: Washington Commanders
teams.headline: Commanders climb to third in the NFC East

stories.text: Commanders beat Eagles 27-10 and climb the power rankings
stories.summary: Washington won for the first time since Week 3, improving to 2-4-1 and sitting two games behind the Giants. The average power ranking rose to 23.8 from 26.2, and eight of nine outlets moved the team up. A win over the Rams on Sunday followed by one against the Giants on Nov. 13 could put Washington atop the division.

stories.text: Defensive line thin, Burks sits Wednesday
stories.summary: Treylon Burks (foot) did not practice, and Terry McLaurin is out for the season on injured reserve. Both starting defensive tackles went on injured reserve, Shy Tuttle (shoulder) was limited, and Jer'Zhan Newton (pectoral) practiced fully and awaits activation. Jayden Daniels (left elbow) was a full participant.

stories.text: Daniels steadies the offense after a 10-0 hole
stories.summary: Jayden Daniels threw for 217 yards and a touchdown to Stefon Diggs, and he totaled 240 yards in the win. He led an 89-yard drive going 5 of 6, and the team says he has thrown no interceptions this season. Washington scored 27 unanswered points after falling behind 10-0.

stories.text: +7: Washington's turnover margin, tied for first in the NFL
stories.summary: The Commanders rank first in turnover differential even though they sit 20th in total offense and total defense. Their weak spots are third downs, where the offense ranks 31st and the defense 25th. The Rams are tied for 26th at minus-4.

stories.text: Vs. Rams, Sunday 1 p.m. ET on Fox
stories.summary: Washington hosts the Rams, who rank fourth in total offense behind Matthew Stafford's 2,146 passing yards. The Commanders have not beaten the Rams at home since 2015. Watch the depleted defensive line against Kyren Williams and the run game, then a Thursday night trip to the Giants on Nov. 13.

teams.name: Chicago Bears
teams.headline: Simmons makes instant impact in Bears rout

stories.text: Jeffery Simmons sacks Seattle in Bears debut, Chicago rolls 34-17
stories.summary: Chicago traded for Simmons last Thursday and he played Monday night like he had been there all year. He sacked Sam Darnold on the opening drive and added six tackles, three pressures and a pass defensed. The Bears improved to 6-2 and sit a half game behind Minnesota in the NFC North.

stories.text: Monangai out again as Bears walk through Wednesday
stories.summary: Running back Kyle Monangai has missed four straight games with a turf toe injury and was estimated out on the Wednesday report. Left tackle Theo Benedet (shoulder) and defensive tackle Grady Jarrett (groin) would not have practiced, and the team placed DT Kentavius Street (knee) on injured reserve. Ben Johnson said the team will see over the week who can go Sunday.

stories.text: Caleb Williams stays clean in Seattle with 247 yards and a score
stories.summary: Williams completed 24 of 34 passes for 247 yards and a 1-yard touchdown to Luther Burden on the opening drive. He turned the ball over zero times and took one sack. Chicago is 3-0 in his starts since he came back from a hamstring injury in Week 6.

stories.text: 1: third-down conversion Seattle allowed on 11 tries
stories.summary: Chicago's defense held the Seahawks to a 1-for-11 mark on third down and 252 total yards. Seattle ran for only 81 yards. D'Andre Swift scored three second-half touchdowns on short runs to finish the job.

stories.text: Buccaneers visit Soldier Field on Sunday night
stories.summary: Tampa Bay (3-5) plays at Chicago on Sunday, Nov. 8 at 8:20 p.m. ET on NBC. Caleb Williams and Baker Mayfield, both former No. 1 overall picks, meet for the first time. Bucky Irving ranks fourth in the NFL with 728 rushing yards, so watch how the Bears' run defense handles him.

teams.name: Detroit Lions
teams.headline: Lions end Vikings' unbeaten run, 19-15

stories.text: Lions hand Minnesota its first loss, 19-15 at Ford Field
stories.summary: Jameson Williams caught a 7-yard touchdown from Jared Goff in the fourth quarter to win it. Detroit ran for 230 yards on the Vikings and moved to 5-2, 2-0 in the division. The defense has held opponents to 17.6 points per game during a three-game win streak.

stories.text: Jack Campbell regains movement in legs; Joseph out for Miami
stories.summary: Linebacker Jack Campbell was carted off Sunday with a neck injury and remains in the hospital, but he says he has full movement in his lower body. Safety Kerby Joseph will not play in Miami. Center Cade Mays (ankle), cornerback D.J. Reed (hip) and edge DJ Wonnum (concussion) did not practice Wednesday.

stories.text: Jahmyr Gibbs runs for 153 yards and a 30-yard score
stories.summary: Gibbs carried 23 times against Minnesota and broke a 30-yard touchdown run in the third quarter. He also helped drive the seven-play, 69-yard series that set up the winning score. Sione Vaki added 65 yards on 11 carries.

stories.text: 230: rushing yards Detroit piled up on Minnesota
stories.summary: The Lions ran 39 times for 230 yards and a touchdown. It was the most the Vikings have allowed on the ground in nearly three years. Minnesota missed more than a dozen tackles.

stories.text: Lions travel to Miami on Sunday at 1 p.m. ET
stories.summary: Detroit plays the 1-6 Dolphins on CBS on Sunday, Nov. 8. Juice Scruggs is expected to start at center with Mays hurt. Watch how the defense fills in for Campbell and Joseph.

teams.name: Green Bay Packers
teams.headline: Parsons opens practice window, Thanksgiving target

stories.text: Micah Parsons returns to practice, eyes Thanksgiving-week game
stories.summary: Green Bay opened Parsons' 21-day practice window and he was a limited participant Wednesday. He is recovering from a torn ACL and torn meniscus. Matt LaFleur said Parsons will work in individual drills before ramping up in a couple of weeks, with the Rams game as the target.

stories.text: Parsons limited; Franklin, Glover and Whyle sit out
stories.summary: Linebacker Zaire Franklin (shin), lineman Travis Glover (knee) and tight end Josh Whyle (concussion) did not practice Wednesday. Guard Aaron Banks (knee), running back Chris Brooks (ankle), cornerback Keisean Nixon (groin) and wideout Christian Watson were limited. Parsons is not expected to play Sunday.

stories.text: Jordan Love leads the league in passing yards
stories.summary: Love has 2,246 passing yards, tops in the NFL, and completed 30 passes in the 27-19 win over Carolina. He threw a 24-yard touchdown to Matthew Golden just before halftime and a 4-yard score to Josh Jacobs. Green Bay's pass offense ranks second at 271.0 yards per game.

stories.text: 60.6: rushing yards per game, last in the NFL
stories.summary: Green Bay's ground game is 32nd in the league at 60.6 yards per game. The offense compensates through the air, ranking 18th in total yards and tied for 23rd in points at 21.4 per game. The defense allows 20.5 points a game, 10th best.

stories.text: Packers visit Patriots on Sunday at 4:25 p.m. ET on FOX
stories.summary: Both teams are 5-3 for the game at Gillette Stadium. Green Bay's second-ranked pass offense faces the 13th-ranked pass defense. Watch whether the Packers can find any rushing production against a Patriots run game that ranks 12th.

teams.name: Minnesota Vikings
teams.headline: Vikings take first loss, Murray hamstring in doubt

stories.text: Vikings fall to Detroit for first loss of the season
stories.summary: Minnesota lost 19-15 at Ford Field to drop to 6-1. Kyler Murray threw for 210 yards, two touchdowns and an interception, and the offense gained 266 yards to Detroit's 384. The defense gave up 230 yards on the ground.

stories.text: Murray's sore hamstring leaves Bills game uncertain
stories.summary: Kyler Murray went to the medical tent late Sunday with hamstring tightness and returned. On Monday Kevin O'Connell said it was sore and the team was doing a full evaluation, adding that they were not there yet. Carson Wentz would start if Murray cannot play.

stories.text: Andrew Van Ginkel piles up 2.5 sacks in the loss
stories.summary: Van Ginkel had 2.5 sacks and three quarterback hits at Ford Field. Joshua Metellus led the team with 13 tackles. The pass rush was the bright spot on a day the run defense struggled.

stories.text: 28: catches for Justin Jefferson through seven games
stories.summary: Jefferson has 28 receptions in seven games, a total that leaves Minnesota looking for more big plays through the air. Murray has been sacked three times for 25 yards against Detroit. The offense managed 266 total yards in the loss.

stories.text: Bills visit U.S. Bank Stadium on Monday Night Football
stories.summary: Minnesota (6-1) hosts Buffalo (6-1) on Monday, Nov. 9 at 8:15 p.m. ET on ABC and ESPN. Murray's hamstring is the key question. Josh Allen and the Bills have won three straight.

teams.name: Atlanta Falcons
teams.headline: Pearce set to return in Madrid

stories.text: Pearce set to return against Bengals in Madrid
stories.summary: Edge rusher James Pearce Jr. finishes his eight-game suspension and becomes eligible on Nov. 2. Coach Kevin Stefanski said the plan is for him to play Sunday in Madrid. Pearce had 10.5 sacks as a rookie and joins a pass rush that led the league in pressures entering Week 8.

stories.text: Branch out, Robinson and Deablo limited in Madrid
stories.summary: The Falcons held a walkthrough after landing in Spain and released an estimated report. Receiver Zachariah Branch (hamstring) did not participate and is ruled out. Running back Brian Robinson Jr. (hamstring), linebacker Divine Deablo (forearm) and linebacker Yasir Abdullah (hamstring) were limited. Pearce, Billy Bowman Jr., Beaux Collins and Cameron Williams went full.

stories.text: Bijan Robinson gets 19 carries in a rain-soaked loss
stories.summary: Robinson led the NFL with 780 rushing yards through Week 8, but the Falcons gave him only 19 carries for 76 yards in the 16-0 loss at Tampa Bay. Bucky Irving and Kenny Gainwell each carried more than he did. Atlanta went 0 for 12 on third down and held the ball under 25 minutes.

stories.text: 12.0: Penix's passer rating in the shutout loss
stories.summary: Michael Penix Jr. completed 8 of 24 passes for 125 yards and threw four interceptions, three more than he had all season. Tampa Bay ran for a franchise-record 324 yards behind a defense that took the ball away four times. The Falcons finished with 224 total yards, 76 of them on one late play.

stories.text: Falcons meet the Bengals in Madrid Sunday morning
stories.summary: Atlanta (3-5) plays Cincinnati (5-2) on Sunday, Nov. 8 at 9:30 a.m. ET at the Santiago Bernabeu, on NFL Network. Watch how many snaps Pearce plays and whether Penix bounces back against Joe Burrow, who leads the league in passing yards per game at 302.1.

teams.name: Carolina Panthers
teams.headline: Panthers fire DC Evero after loss

stories.text: Panthers fire defensive coordinator Ejiro Evero
stories.summary: Head coach Dave Canales fired Evero and pass game coordinator Jonathan Cooley after a 27-19 Thursday night loss to Green Bay, which followed a 43-13 loss to Tampa Bay. Defensive line coach Todd Wash is the interim coordinator and play caller. Carolina allowed 70 points in four days.

stories.text: Four Panthers miss estimated practice, Young full
stories.summary: Carolina did not practice Wednesday, so the team released a projection based on Tuesday. Outside linebacker Jaelan Phillips (hamstring), guard Damien Lewis (knee), linebacker Bobby Okereke (foot) and rookie cornerback Will Lee III (hamstring) did not participate. Quarterback Bryce Young (ankle) was full, and lineman Brady Christensen has opened his practice window.

stories.text: Bryce Young takes six sacks against Green Bay
stories.summary: Young was sacked six times in the loss to the Packers and finished with a 36.2 QBR. He said Tuesday that he feels fine and can do everything for the team. He is on the injury report with an ankle issue but practiced fully Wednesday.

stories.text: 12: rushing touchdowns Carolina's defense has allowed
stories.summary: No defense has given up more rushing scores. The Panthers rank 30th in rushing yards allowed per game and 27th in points allowed, while the offense averages 25.4 points, ninth in the league. In Week 1 they gave up 59 points and 552 yards to Chicago.

stories.text: Panthers host the 6-2 Broncos Sunday
stories.summary: Carolina (3-4) hosts Denver (6-2) on Sunday, Nov. 8 at 1:00 p.m. ET at Bank of America Stadium on CBS. Wash calls his first game plan against Bo Nix. The Panthers are 0-4 on the road but 2-2 at home, and rookie Jonah Coleman has taken over as Denver's lead back.

teams.name: New Orleans Saints
teams.headline: Saints fire run game coordinator

stories.text: Saints fire run game coordinator T.J. Paganetti
stories.summary: Coach Kellen Moore made the change after the bye week. Offensive line coach Brendan Nugent now leads the run game structure, and running backs coach Joel Thomas keeps giving input. New Orleans ranks 28th at 86 rushing yards per game, and center Erik McCoy said the move reflects on the whole line.

stories.text: Kamara rests, Tyson and Banks back in limited work
stories.summary: Running back Alvin Kamara did not practice Wednesday (rest, back). Wide receiver Jordyn Tyson (hamstring), tackle Kelvin Banks Jr. (ankle), running back CJ Donaldson, cornerback Martin Emerson Jr. and tackle Asim Richards were limited. Safety Justin Reid (concussion), guard Cesar Ruiz and lineman Nathan Shepherd went full.

stories.text: Chris Olave leads the offense, but production has cooled
stories.summary: Olave has 49 catches for 636 yards through seven games, tops on the team. He has not topped 56 receiving yards in any of his last three games. With Tyson working back from a hamstring injury, the Saints need more from him against Cleveland.

stories.text: 44-6: how first quarters have gone for the Saints
stories.summary: Opponents have outscored New Orleans by that margin in the opening period. The Saints trailed in every game and came back to win only twice, at Baltimore and at the Giants. Quarterback Tyler Shough has thrown 13 touchdowns and six interceptions.

stories.text: Saints seek first home win against Browns
stories.summary: New Orleans (2-5) hosts Cleveland (5-3) on Sunday, Nov. 8 at 1:00 p.m. ET at the Caesars Superdome on CBS. The Saints have not won at home this season. Browns quarterback Deshaun Watson (concussion) did not practice Wednesday.

teams.name: Tampa Bay Buccaneers
teams.headline: Bucs win 16-0 without a completion

stories.text: Bucs shut out Falcons without a completed pass
stories.summary: Baker Mayfield returned from a dislocated right thumb and went 0 for 3 in heavy rain, yet Tampa Bay won 16-0. It was the first win by a team with no completions since the 1974 Bills. The Bucs ran for 324 yards and intercepted Michael Penix Jr. four times.

stories.text: Diaby, Egbuka and Roberts sit out Wednesday
stories.summary: Outside linebacker Yaya Diaby (knee), receiver Emeka Egbuka (foot) and lineman Elijah Roberts (personal) did not participate. Running back Kenneth Gainwell (hip) and safety Tykee Smith (ankle) were limited. Quarterback Baker Mayfield (right thumb) practiced fully.

stories.text: Bucky Irving runs for 170 yards on 27 carries
stories.summary: Irving set a career high in carries and scored the only touchdown, a four-yard run in the third quarter. He and Gainwell, who ran for 140, both topped 100 yards in one game, a first for the franchise since Mike Alstott and Warrick Dunn in 1998. Irving also fumbled at the one-yard line.

stories.text: 324: rushing yards, a Bucs single-game record
stories.summary: Tampa Bay set the franchise mark in the win over Atlanta. Kicker Chase McLaughlin made field goals from 46, 34 and 42 yards and is 19 for 19 this year. The shutout was the Bucs' first since the 2023 season finale.

stories.text: Bucs visit the Bears on Sunday Night Football
stories.summary: Tampa Bay (3-5) plays at Chicago (6-2) on Sunday, Nov. 8 at Soldier Field on NBC, with kickoff listed at 8:20 p.m. ET by the team. Watch whether Mayfield and the passing game get on track after the zero-completion game, with Egbuka's foot a question.

teams.name: Arizona Cardinals
teams.headline: Minshew takes over at QB for Seattle trip

stories.text: Cardinals bench Brissett, ride Minshew to overtime win and a new job
stories.summary: Arizona trailed Dallas 17-3 late in the third quarter when the staff pulled Jacoby Brissett, who had started every game. Gardner Minshew II went 17 of 23 for 188 yards and three touchdowns, and the Cardinals won 33-30 in overtime. Minshew is now the Week 9 starter at Seattle, with rookie Carson Beck as his backup.

stories.text: Eight Cardinals sit out Wednesday, Wilson limited with ribs
stories.summary: Budda Baker, Hjalte Froholdt, Josh Sweat and Isaac Seumalo got rest days, while Jayden Williams (knee), Jon Gaines II (ankle), Bam Knight (concussion) and Jacoby Brissett did not practice. Michael Wilson, hurt against Dallas, was limited with a rib injury and a non-contact jersey. Isaiah Adams (ankle) returned in a limited role and the team opened his 21-day practice window.

stories.text: Tyler Allgeier ran for 143 of his 147 yards after halftime
stories.summary: Allgeier opened the Cardinals' comeback in Dallas with a 63-yard run and finished with 147 rushing yards, nearly all of it in the second half. He also caught a touchdown pass. He gives Minshew a ground game to lean on at Lumen Field on Sunday.

stories.text: 111: Michael Wilson's receiving yards on two broken ribs
stories.summary: Wilson caught eight passes for 111 yards and a touchdown against Dallas while playing through a rib injury, according to Raising Zona. His Sunday status depends on how the ribs hold up this week.

stories.text: At Seattle on Sunday, 4:25 p.m. ET on FOX
stories.summary: Arizona visits Lumen Field for a 4:25 p.m. ET kickoff on FOX. Seattle beat the Cardinals 31-7 in Week 2 behind Drew Lock, who is expected to start again with Sam Darnold out. Watch whether Arizona's secondary can handle Jaxon Smith-Njigba.

teams.name: Los Angeles Rams
teams.headline: Rams chase first winning record at Washington

stories.text: Rams beat winless Chargers 24-9 for a second straight win
stories.summary: The Rams started slowly, with no first downs on their first three possessions, then pulled away behind two takeaways and a steady running game. Blake Corum ran for 73 yards and a touchdown, and Kyren Williams added a score. At 4-4, Los Angeles can climb above .500 for the first time this season at Washington on Sunday.

stories.text: Rams lose cornerback Jaylen Watson for the season
stories.summary: Watson needs shoulder surgery and goes to injured reserve, and Sean McVay called it a big blow. Myles Garrett (knee) opened his 21-day practice window and was limited Wednesday. Trent McDuffie did not practice, while Joe Cardona, Kam Curl and Colby Parkinson also sat out. Matthew Stafford was a full participant.

stories.text: Puka Nacua caught 11 passes and a screen touchdown against the Chargers
stories.summary: Nacua finished with 11 catches for 80 yards and a touchdown in the 24-9 win. He said the team has to keep building and cannot relax after two wins. Washington's game plan will start with him.

stories.text: 13 of 14: Stafford on throws released in under 2.5 seconds
stories.summary: Matthew Stafford went 13 of 14 for 94 yards and a touchdown on quick throws against the Chargers, per Football Nation. He finished 17 of 25 for 157 yards with one touchdown and one interception. The quick game kept Los Angeles on schedule while the offense found its rhythm.

stories.text: At Washington on Sunday, 1:00 p.m. ET on FOX
stories.summary: The Rams (4-4) visit the Commanders (2-4-1) at Northwest Stadium for a 1:00 p.m. ET kickoff on FOX. Washington had five sacks against Philadelphia last week and has a five-game takeaway streak. Watch how the Rams protect Stafford and whether Garrett plays.

teams.name: San Francisco 49ers
teams.headline: Buckner is back as 49ers return from bye

stories.text: 49ers trade a fourth-round pick to bring back DeForest Buckner
stories.summary: San Francisco sent a 2027 fourth-round pick to Indianapolis for Buckner, the seventh overall pick in 2016. Shanahan named defensive line and receiver as the obvious injury spots. Kyle Shanahan said Deebo Samuel, Nick Bosa, C.J. West, Mike Evans and Demarcus Robinson had a chance to return by Week 9.

stories.text: Evans and McCaffrey miss first practice of Raiders week
stories.summary: Mike Evans (Achilles tendinitis), Christian McCaffrey (hamstring), Deebo Samuel (hamstring) and Siran Neal (knee and foot) did not practice Wednesday. Shanahan said the team wants Evans fully healthy before he plays. McCaffrey got hurt against Atlanta, left early and later came back. CBS Sports also listed Trent Williams as a non-participant, a detail SI did not report.

stories.text: Brock Purdy looks to clean up after two interceptions in Atlanta
stories.summary: Purdy threw a fourth-quarter pick to Jessie Bates III and another to rookie Kendal Daniels on a third-and-9 with the lead in reach, in a 29-20 loss. The 49ers were missing their top five receivers. He gets a reset against the Raiders on Sunday.

stories.text: 4: Buckner's sacks with Indianapolis before the trade
stories.summary: Buckner had four sacks this season for the Colts before the deal, per Sports Illustrated. San Francisco's pass rush went quiet in the second half against Atlanta, so he arrives where the team needs help most.

stories.text: Raiders on Sunday, 4:25 p.m. ET on FOX
stories.summary: The 49ers (6-1) play the Raiders on Sunday at 4:25 p.m. ET on FOX after their bye. Watch which of Bosa, Evans, Samuel and McCaffrey are available, and how Buckner fits in on the defensive line.

teams.name: Seattle Seahawks
teams.headline: Darnold out, Lock starts against Arizona

stories.text: Sam Darnold is out with a quad injury, Drew Lock to start
stories.summary: Darnold will miss Sunday's game against Arizona with quad and rib injuries, so Lock steps in coming off a 34-17 Monday night loss to Chicago. Lock threw for 235 yards and three touchdowns in Seattle's 31-7 win over the Cardinals in Week 2. Seattle is 4-4.

stories.text: Cross, Shaheed and Leonard Williams miss Wednesday's practice
stories.summary: Charles Cross (ankle), Rashid Shaheed (knee), Leonard Williams (stinger), Connor O'Toole (foot) and Brandon Pili (back) did not practice. Quenton Nelson (knee), Uchenna Nwosu (ankle) and Lock (right elbow) were limited. Seattle held a walkthrough, so the designations are estimates.

stories.text: Jaxon Smith-Njigba owns 51.5 percent of Seattle's receiving yards
stories.summary: Smith-Njigba caught six passes for 118 yards against Chicago, his seventh 100-yard game in eight weeks. He has 985 yards, 259 more than any other player in the league. That is the second most through eight games in the Super Bowl era.

stories.text: 1 of 11: Seattle's third-down conversions against the Bears
stories.summary: The Seahawks converted one third down in 11 tries a week after going 11 of 16 against Kansas City. The Bears gained 363 yards, the most any Seattle opponent has gained this season. The defense had allowed a league-low 233.9 yards per game before Monday.

stories.text: Cardinals on Sunday, 4:25 p.m. ET on FOX
stories.summary: Seattle hosts Arizona at Lumen Field with a 4:25 p.m. ET kickoff on FOX. Mike Macdonald wants the team to recapture its identity after the Bears loss, including a run defense that allowed three short second-half touchdowns. Watch the quarterback spot and the offensive line.
